name: Cloud / DevOps
tagline: Excellent pay and strong demand — but almost never a first job.
description: Cloud and DevOps roles pay well and are heavily remote. The honest catch: DevOps is a senior discipline built on top of systems administration, networking, and scripting. Nobody is hired as a DevOps engineer from zero. The realistic entry point is cloud support or a junior cloud/infrastructure role, and the fundamentals certs are cheap and genuinely useful early.
avgTimeline: 18–30 months, typically via IT support or sysadmin work first

salaryRange.note: Cloud support associate / junior cloud engineer range. Full DevOps and cloud engineer roles commonly reach $110K–160K+, but that's 3–5 years in, not entry. AWS support roles at the associate level are a well-known on-ramp.

remoteFriendly.note: One of the most remote-friendly areas in tech — the infrastructure is in someone else's data center by definition. On-call rotations are standard and should be asked about in interviews.

realityCheck: The certification-to-job gap is wider here than anywhere else. An AWS Solutions Architect certificate with no operations experience produces very few interviews, because the work is judgment about running systems, which a multiple-choice exam cannot demonstrate. Certs plus a real support job plus a public infrastructure project is the combination that works.
whyItFits: This path suits people who like automating repetitive work out of existence. If the thing that bothered you about warehouse work was watching the same manual process happen a hundred times a day, that instinct is exactly what this field pays for.

motivation.quote: The first time a script you wrote replaces four hours of somebody's week, you understand the whole field.
motivation.story: A well-worn route in: help desk for a year, get AWS Cloud Practitioner while there, automate something visible internally (patching, onboarding, backup verification) with a script, then apply to cloud support roles at AWS, Azure, or a managed service provider. Cloud support at a hyperscaler is a demanding, high-volume job that hires people without degrees and puts a name-brand cloud provider on your resume.
motivation.source: Composite of the pattern described in r/AWSCertifications and r/devops career threads

interviewPrep.question: What's the difference between IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS?
interviewPrep.why: Foundational and always asked. Give examples: EC2 (IaaS), App Service or Elastic Beanstalk (PaaS), Microsoft 365 (SaaS).

interviewPrep.question: A customer says their EC2 instance is unreachable. How do you troubleshoot?
interviewPrep.why: The classic cloud support question. Structure: instance state, security groups, network ACLs, route tables, subnet/IGW config, key pair, OS-level firewall. Say you'd check from broad to narrow.

interviewPrep.question: Explain the difference between object storage and block storage.
interviewPrep.why: S3 vs EBS. Object storage: flat, HTTP API, cheap, great for backups and static assets. Block storage: attached to one instance, behaves like a disk.

interviewPrep.question: What is infrastructure as code and why does it matter?
interviewPrep.why: Terraform or CloudFormation. Key points: reproducibility, version control, code review for infrastructure changes, no snowflake servers built by hand.

interviewPrep.question: What problem does Docker solve?
interviewPrep.why: Consistent runtime environments across machines. Mention the difference from a VM (shared kernel, lighter, faster startup).

interviewPrep.question: How would you reduce a cloud bill that's growing unexpectedly?
interviewPrep.why: Cost is a real part of the job. Find unused resources, right-size instances, check storage tiers and data transfer, use reserved or spot capacity, set up billing alerts and tagging.

interviewPrep.question: How would you handle being paged at 3am for a service that's down?
interviewPrep.why: They're checking temperament. Answer: follow the runbook, restore service before diagnosing root cause, communicate status, write the postmortem afterward.

steps.title: Get Linux and networking fundamentals
steps.description: Everything in cloud runs on Linux and talks over a network. Before touching AWS, be comfortable with the command line, SSH, file permissions, systemd services, and log files, and understand IP addressing, subnets, DNS, and firewalls. Skipping this is why people with certs still can't do the work.
steps.outcome: You can administer a Linux server over SSH without a GUI.
steps.resumeBullet: Proficient with Linux system administration: shell, SSH, permissions, systemd service management, and log analysis.

resources.name: OverTheWire: Bandit
resources.notes: Free. The fastest way to become genuinely comfortable in a terminal.

resources.name: Linux Journey
resources.notes: Free, structured beginner Linux curriculum.

resources.name: Practical Networking — free fundamentals series
resources.notes: Free. Covers the networking concepts cloud work assumes you already have.

steps.title: Pass a cloud fundamentals certification
steps.description: AWS Cloud Practitioner ($100) or Microsoft Azure Fundamentals AZ-900 ($99) are the two cheapest genuinely-useful certs in tech. Pick based on your local job market — search job listings in your area for 'AWS' vs 'Azure' and count. Government, healthcare, and traditional enterprise skew Azure; startups and tech companies skew AWS.
steps.costNote: PAID but cheap: AWS Cloud Practitioner is $100; Azure AZ-900 is $99 (reduced from $165). Microsoft regularly runs free-voucher promotions through Virtual Training Days — check before paying.
steps.outcome: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner or Azure Fundamentals certified.
steps.resumeBullet: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (or Microsoft Azure Fundamentals) — cloud service models, core infrastructure services, security model, and cost management.

resources.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (official)
resources.notes: PAID, $100 plus tax. Free official prep is available on AWS Skill Builder.

resources.name: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals AZ-900 (official)
resources.notes: PAID, $99 in the US. Microsoft Virtual Training Days sometimes include a free exam voucher — worth watching for.

resources.name: AWS Skill Builder (free tier)
resources.notes: Free official AWS training including full Cloud Practitioner prep.

resources.name: Microsoft Learn (free AZ-900 path)
resources.notes: Free official learning path, sufficient to pass without paid training.

steps.title: Build something real in a free-tier cloud account
steps.description: Deploy an actual application to the cloud yourself: a VM behind a load balancer, a static site on object storage with a CDN, a database, monitoring, and a budget alarm so you don't get a surprise bill. Set the billing alert first — this is the step where people accidentally spend money.
steps.costNote: Nearly free if you stay inside free tiers and shut resources down — budget $0–15 total for accidents. Set a billing alarm at $5 on day one, before you create anything.
steps.outcome: A live application you deployed and can explain the architecture of.
steps.resumeBullet: Deployed and operated a multi-tier application on AWS/Azure: compute, managed database, object storage, load balancing, monitoring, and cost alerting.

resources.name: AWS Free Tier
resources.notes: Free tier with limits. Read what expires after 12 months, and set a billing alarm immediately.

resources.name: Azure free account
resources.notes: Free credits for the first 30 days plus always-free service tiers.

resources.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free tier
resources.notes: Free. The most generous permanently-free compute allocation of the major clouds — useful for a lab that never expires.

resources.name: AWS Cloud Quest (free gamified labs)
resources.notes: Free role-playing labs in a real AWS environment.

steps.title: Learn scripting and automation
steps.description: Bash for glue, Python for anything with logic, and enough YAML to be dangerous. The bar is not 'software engineer' — it's being able to write a 100-line script that automates a task reliably and handles errors. Automate something in your current job, even if your current job is retail: a spreadsheet report, a schedule parser, anything.
steps.outcome: You automate tasks instead of repeating them.
steps.resumeBullet: Automated operational tasks with Python and Bash scripting, including scheduled jobs, API integrations, and error handling/logging.

resources.name: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python (free online)
resources.notes: Free to read online. Exactly the right level for operations scripting.

resources.name: Google IT Automation with Python Certificate (Coursera)
resources.notes: PAID: $49/month. Optional — Automate the Boring Stuff covers similar ground free. Financial aid is available.

resources.name: Bash scripting guide (Linux Documentation Project)
resources.notes: Free reference. Dated in style, still accurate.

steps.title: Learn containers, IaC, and CI/CD
steps.description: The three technologies that define modern operations work: Docker (package an application with its dependencies), Terraform (define infrastructure as version-controlled code), and a CI/CD pipeline (GitHub Actions is free and the easiest starting point). Kubernetes can wait — learn it after you have a job that uses it.
steps.costNote: Free. Docker Desktop is free for personal use and small businesses, Terraform's CLI is free, GitHub Actions is free for public repositories.
steps.outcome: You can containerize an app, define its infrastructure in code, and deploy it automatically on push.
steps.resumeBullet: Built CI/CD pipelines with GitHub Actions, containerized applications with Docker, and provisioned cloud infrastructure as code with Terraform.

resources.name: Docker official getting started guide
resources.notes: Free official documentation.

resources.name: HashiCorp Terraform tutorials
resources.notes: Free official hands-on tutorials.

resources.name: GitHub Actions documentation
resources.notes: Free, and free to run on public repositories.

resources.name: roadmap.sh DevOps roadmap
resources.notes: Free. A good map of what exists and what order to learn it in — treat it as a map, not a checklist to complete.

steps.title: An associate-level cloud certification
steps.description: AWS Solutions Architect Associate or Azure Administrator (AZ-104) is the next credential tier. Worth it once you have hands-on experience to attach it to — worth much less before that. If you're already working in IT, ask whether your employer will pay for it; many will.
steps.costNote: PAID: AWS associate-level exams are $150; Azure AZ-104 is $165. Both are frequently covered by employers. Do the fundamentals cert and the hands-on project first.
steps.resumeBullet: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (or Azure Administrator AZ-104): architecture design, networking, identity, storage, and cost optimization.

resources.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate
resources.notes: PAID, $150. Confirm price and exam version before booking.

resources.name: Microsoft Certified: Azure Administrator Associate (AZ-104)
resources.notes: PAID, $165 in the US.

resources.name: Adrian Cantrill / Stephane Maarek courses
resources.notes: PAID, roughly $40–60 (Cantrill) or $15–20 on Udemy sale (Maarek). Both are widely regarded as the best paid AWS training. Optional.

steps.title: Enter through cloud support or an ops-adjacent role
steps.description: Target cloud support associate roles (AWS and Microsoft both hire these in volume and do not require degrees), NOC and infrastructure support jobs, or an internal move at your current employer. These roles put you on real production systems, which is the missing ingredient every DevOps posting is actually screening for.
steps.outcome: A cloud or infrastructure role on production systems.

resources.name: AWS careers — Cloud Support Associate
resources.notes: Free. AWS hires cloud support associates continuously, in several US locations and remotely, without requiring a degree.

resources.name: Microsoft careers — support engineering
resources.notes: Free. Azure support engineer roles are a comparable on-ramp.

resources.name: r/devops — 'how do I get started' threads
resources.notes: Free. The community is consistent and blunt: DevOps is not an entry-level job. Read that before spending on advanced certs.
